summary: Describes the `undef()` Jinja2 function (since 2.12), which returns an AnsibleUndefined object to undefine lower-precedence variables, for example overriding a host variable for one block. It takes an optional `hint` shown when DEFAULT_UNDEFINED_VAR_BEHAVIOR errors.
questions: How do I unset a host variable for just one block of tasks?
What does undef() do in Ansible?
How do I give a custom error message for an undefined variable?
Can I undefine a variable that was set at a lower precedence?

answer_card.title: Undefine variables with undef()
answer_card.answer_md:
Added in 2.12. `undef()` returns an `AnsibleUndefined` object (derived from `jinja2.StrictUndefined`), which lets you undefine variables of lower precedence, e.g. for one block:

```yaml
- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: no
  module_defaults:
    group/ns.col.auth: "{{ vaulted_credentials | default({}) }}"
  tasks:
    - ns.col.module1:
    - name: override host variable
      vars:
        vaulted_credentials: "{{ undef() }}"
      block:
        - ns.col.module1:
```
Optional argument `hint`: a custom message about the undefined variable, shown when `DEFAULT_UNDEFINED_VAR_BEHAVIOR` is configured to error.
